name: Vietnam

findings.reversal_of: Viettel's prior use of Huawei as a network equipment supplier, not extended to its 5G rollout
findings.summary: Viettel left Huawei off its 5G supplier list, with its chief executive citing security doubts about Huawei and choosing Ericsson and Nokia instead; other leading carriers were also reported avoiding Huawei 5G gear.

sources.note: relays Bloomberg interview with Viettel CEO

findings.analyst_inference: Coded as an exclusion (reversal) rather than a formal ban: no regulator decision found. Tier 3 is a judgment for the procurement relationship not extended; the existing 4G Huawei base was not reported removed.

findings.summary: Ericsson and Nokia hold contracts for Vietnam's 5G core network infrastructure; Viettel had chosen the two Nordic vendors for its 5G rollout in 2019.
findings.analyst_inference: Contract dates, values and which operators beyond Viettel hold Ericsson/Nokia core contracts are not stated in the sources; date left null.

findings.summary: A consortium including Huawei won a 5G equipment contract worth about $23 million in Vietnam, weeks after US tariffs on Vietnamese goods were announced, per tender data and people familiar cited by Reuters.
findings.analyst_inference: Buying operator not named in the source. Reuters frames the award as following warming China ties after US tariffs; causation is not established.

findings.summary: ZTE won at least two contracts for 5G antennas in Vietnam during 2025, together worth more than $20 million, one awarded in late November 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Announced value left null because the source gives only a lower bound (more than $20 million). Buying operator(s) not named.

findings.summary: Huawei signed an agreement with Viettel on 5G technology transfer in June 2025, according to Vietnam's defence ministry as reported by Reuters; Huawei also lost several 5G tenders that year.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 2 (framework/technology-transfer agreement) since no equipment purchase is described. Viettel is military-owned, so the defence ministry is the reporting authority.

findings.controller: Asia Link Cable consortium (incl. China Telecom Global, Singtel, Globe, DITO, UNN)
findings.summary: FPT Telecom committed about $87 million to the roughly 6,000 km Asia Link Cable, whose consortium includes China Telecom Global alongside Singaporean, Philippine and Bruneian carriers.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: control is shared across a multinational consortium in which a PRC state carrier participates; the cable supplier is not named and no Vietnamese landing point is given in the source.

findings.summary: Viettel opened an AI-ready data centre at Hoa Lac Hi-Tech Park, Hanoi, with up to 30 MW capacity, described as the largest in Vietnam and its 14th facility.

sources.note: outlet of the Hanoi People's Committee; state-affiliated

findings.analyst_inference: Single S2 source plus a state-affiliated outlet, so not marked corroborated under the rule; the opening itself is low-controversy. Equipment vendors not named.

findings.summary: G42 signed a long-term framework agreement with an FPT–Viet Thai consortium to invest in, build and operate hyperscale data centres in Vietnam, with up to $1 billion expected for sovereign AI and cloud infrastructure.

sources.note: company release by a party to the deal

findings.analyst_inference: Follows a July 2025 reported proposal by G42 and partners for a ~$2 billion hyperscale data centre in Ho Chi Minh City (W.Media 2025-07-11, AGBI); the $2bn figure was not carried forward and is not counted here. No site, capacity or investment decision yet.

findings.summary: FPT's AI Factory in Vietnam serves customers on Nvidia HGX H100 and H200 platforms and announced an Nvidia HGX B300 build-out; it began from an April 2024 $200 million MOU with Nvidia.
findings.analyst_inference: $200 million is the MOU announcement figure, not verified spend. GPU counts not disclosed; FPT infrastructure spans Vietnam and Japan, so the Vietnam share is unknown. B300 systems not yet live as of the release.

findings.summary: Viettel reports operating a cluster of 22 Nvidia DGX B200 systems and partnering with Nvidia on sovereign AI infrastructure and Vietnamese foundation models.

sources.note: states Viettel's AI data centre already used Nvidia technology

findings.analyst_inference: Instrument form of the Viettel–Nvidia partnership not stated; tier 5 reflects the reported operating cluster only, which lacks S1/S2 confirmation.

findings.summary: Vietnam's government signed an agreement with Nvidia to set up an AI research and development centre and expand a Viettel-owned AI data centre; no value was disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Legal form of the agreement is unspecified; coded tier 1. Not corroborated (no S1/S2 source found).

findings.summary: Nvidia acquired VinBrain, Vingroup's healthcare AI unit, confirmed at a December 2024 meeting with the Vietnamese government; terms were not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 treats the acquisition as a closed transaction; Vingroup had invested over $126 million in VinBrain, which is not the deal price.

findings.summary: Viettel AI trained VT-Super-120B, a 120-billion-parameter Vietnamese sovereign model built on Nvidia's open Nemotron 3 Super architecture; no public release was described.

sources.note: own announcement of a military-owned firm; treated as corporate/state-affiliated

findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic because Viettel controls the fine-tuned weights; the base is US-origin open weights (Nvidia Nemotron), a dependency on the US ecosystem rather than vendor control. Tier 2 as developed and benchmarked but not deployed at scale.

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced in facility searches; search budget spent on higher-priority layers

research_gaps: Which operator(s) bought the April 2025 Huawei-consortium 5G equipment and the ZTE antenna contracts? Check Vietnamese tender portals.
Text and status of the June 2025 Huawei–Viettel 5G technology-transfer agreement (defence ministry source).
Safe-city / public-security camera procurement: one search found only privacy coverage, no vendor-specific award records for Hikvision, Dahua or Huawei.
Status of the G42–FPT–Viet Thai hyperscale project: site, capacity, investment certificate, construction start.
Viettel's Ho Chi Minh City large data-centre groundbreaking (W.Media) not reviewed; capacity and equipment vendors unknown.
Builders/suppliers of Vietnam's newer submarine cables (ALC, ADC, SJC2) and any HMN Technologies role; ALC Vietnamese landing point.
S1/S2 confirmation of Viettel's 22-system DGX B200 cluster and any BIS licences for Vietnam-bound advanced accelerators.
Government adoption of foreign frontier models (OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen) in Vietnamese public services was not searched.
